transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because I... I barely sleep in any useful way anymore. I'll just lie awake replaying client models in my head. And then I end up waking up at 3 or 4 in the morning with my stomach completely tight, and I just go to work feeling like I never actually rested at all.
Besides your thoughts about work, do you find yourself worrying excessively about several different things in your life—like health, family, or finances—and having a hard time controlling that worry?

No, not really. I mean... I don't sit around stressing about my health or my family. And finances are fine, I deal with that all day anyway. It's really just the work stuff that loops in my head when I'm trying to sleep. So, no, I wouldn't say I worry about a bunch of different things.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or hopeless most of the day, or losing interest or pleasure in things you'd normally enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Most days I just move through the office, and even my apartment, with this... this heavy, gray feeling. It's like I'm really just going through the motions. Honestly, half the time I'm just trying not to cry when someone asks me a completely normal question.
Can you tell me how long you've been feeling this way, and whether it started around a particular event or change in your life, like a new job or stressor?

It's been... well, it's been going on for about three years now. It started right around the time our company went through a merger and they completely reorganized the Caribbean-market division I work in. That's when things really shifted for me, and I've just felt this way ever since.

Over these three years, have you felt this way pretty much continuously without a break, or have there been times when you felt essentially back to normal, and other times when things got noticeably worse than your usual baseline?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I mean... it feels like it's been pretty much continuous. I don't remember any time over the last three years where I felt completely back to normal. But I also haven't really noticed if there were specific times it got drastically worse than my usual baseline, either. It all just kind of blends together into one long stretch of feeling this way.
During this time, have you also noticed changes in your appetite or weight, trouble concentrating, or any thoughts of death or wanting to hurt yourself?

My weight and appetite are pretty much the same, and no, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself. But the concentration... yes, that's been really hard. 

At work, spreadsheets that used to be second nature to me now take hours. I just... I lose the thread of what I'm looking at. I end up rereading the same financial assumptions over and over again, and even after all that, I still worry I've missed something completely obvious right before I have to give a presentation. It's just very hard to keep my focus.
Over these past few years, have you also noticed feeling unusually tired or low on energy most days, even when you haven't exerted yourself much?
No, not really. I mean, I'm tired at the end of the day, but I think that's just normal tiredness from working. I haven't noticed feeling unusually exhausted or having low energy most days, no.
During this time, have you experienced feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt about things, and if so, how intense or overwhelming have those feelings been?

I wouldn't say I feel a lot of excessive guilt, but... the feelings of worthlessness are definitely there, and they can be pretty intense. It mostly happens at work. 

Like, if a manager just questions one of my projections, I don't just see it as a normal work conversation anymore. I immediately hear it as confirmation that I'm not as sharp as I used to be. I just... I get this overwhelming feeling that everyone around me can clearly see that I'm failing. It's really hard to shake that off once it hits me.

Within these three years, has there ever been a stretch of at least two weeks where your symptoms became noticeably more severe or numerous all at once - for example, several of these problems (mood, concentration, worthlessness) hitting hard together - compared to how you've been feeling on average?

No, I don't think so. It's just been a steady, heavy feeling, pretty much the same day in and day out. I haven't noticed a specific couple of weeks where everything suddenly got worse or piled on all at once. It's more of a constant struggle rather than having sudden drops.
